note: Famous trees Commons has a category for and we do not map. Found by scripts/famous_trees.py; each one already has photographs and usually coordinates, so the expensive half of a research pass is done. Not verified by us, not published. Verified and written 2026-09-07: Bilu Sacred Tree passed the single-tree-destination test and shipped as a new place, bilu (blu_001), a Taiwan fir over 3,000 years old on the Central Cross-Island Highway; not confused with the original Alishan Sacred Tree (a different, unlisted tree), which was cut down in 1998 after storm damage and is not a candidate here. Verified and written 2026-09-08 (verification pass on the remaining four batch candidates): Takeshi Kaneshiro Tree shipped as its own place, Chishang (csg_001), a c.50-year-old bishop wood on Mr. Brown Avenue in Taitung County, famous from a 2013 EVA Air ad and toppled/restored after Typhoon Matmo in 2014. The two Sianglin Sacred Tree leads (150 m apart) were confirmed as the same tree, Alishan's publicly-voted second-generation Sacred Tree, and folded into one entry, Alishan (alh_001), age disputed between an old 2,300-year figure and a 2022 university re-dating to about 626 years for the main trunk (it is a fused/composite tree). Couple Trees (the Tataka husband-and-wife trees near Yushan) moved to blocked: confirmed dead since a 1963 forest fire. Xiangyang Famous Tree stays a lead: alive and genuinely ancient but reached only via a permit-gated overnight trek, so it fails the day-trip/single-tree-destination test for now.

leads.name: Xiangyang Famous Tree
leads.note: Real, alive, well-documented Yushan cypress (Juniperus squamata subsp. morrisonicola) estimated 700-800 years old, but it sits at 3,300 m on DAY TWO of the multi-day, permit-gated Jiaming Lake National Trail out of Xiangyang National Forest Recreation Area, reachable only via an overnight wilderness trek with a mountain entry permit filed in advance. Fails the day-trip standard and the single-tree-destination test: hikers travel for Jiaming Lake, and this tree (locally nicknamed the 'thousand-year-old grandfather', officially a female specimen since 2021 research) is a highlight along the way rather than the reason for the trip. Left as a lead rather than blocked outright in case a future pass finds evidence that demand centres on the tree itself rather than the lake. Checked 2026-09-08.

blocked.name: Prayer trees in Taiwan
blocked.reason: Commons category name, not one tree: its photos show a wish tree at a Taipei convention center, an unlabeled site, and a prayer tree at Yuanbao Temple in Taichung, unrelated sites scattered across the island. Fails the one-collectible-point rule (whole-country category, not an avenue or ensemble with one place to stand). Checked 2026-09-08, no verify pass dispatched.

blocked.name: Couple Trees
blocked.reason: DEAD, confirmed by two sources (English and Chinese coverage of Tataka/塔塔加夫妻樹, Yushan National Park): two Formosan cypress trunks killed by a forest fire in 1963, standing since only as bleached dead wood at 2,478 m elevation on the New Central Cross-Island Highway near the Yushan trailhead (coordinates match Wikidata Q10930747, 23.5126, 120.8906, within 20 m of this lead). Fails the never-a-dead-tree-as-an-entry rule outright, however famous the remains. Checked 2026-09-08.
